subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Mechanical Clock: Precision Changes Everything
description: A 60-second lesson on The Mechanical Clock: Precision Changes Everything.

hook.text: Before clocks, a medieval worker's day was defined by sunrise and sunset. Time was approximate.

buildup.text: Around 1300, European monks built the first mechanical clocks using escapement mechanisms.

discovery.text: The escapement releases energy in tiny, equal ticks. It converts continuous force into measured time.

twist.text: Clocks created the concept of the hour as a fixed unit. Before that, daytime hours were longer in summer.

climax.text: Factories, railways, and global trade all depend on precise timekeeping born from a medieval gear.

punchline.text: One gear mechanism changed how civilization works.

quiz.question: What key mechanism made mechanical clocks possible?
options: A pendulum that swings at a constant rate
An escapement that releases energy in equal ticks
A spring that unwinds at a steady speed
